scenes.headline: How Needle 3 turns one checkpoint into many models
scenes.sub: Cactus's sliceable 121M tool-calling model: any depth from 2 to 20 layers.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rhubarb! Needle 3 is Cactus's tiny tool-calling model. Slice its twenty layers to any depth, down to two, and it still works. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Train one 20-layer stack so that every nested subset of its blocks is a standalone model: nineteen models for the storage cost of one.
scenes.say: The idea: train one stack so every nested subset of its blocks works as a model. Nineteen models, for the storage of one.

scenes.title: Why you can't just cut a transformer

left.title: Truncate a normal model
items: Each block leans on specific others
Cut at layer 8 and the load path breaks
left.say: Cut an ordinary transformer in half and it breaks. Each block learned to lean on specific others.

right.title: Train the ladder in
items: No single block can become load-bearing
Early blocks are pushed to do real work
Full depth improves too: 1.958 vs 2.037 loss
right.say: Train every depth together and no block can become load-bearing. Even the full model beat an identical control.

items.say: Fix one order: first and last blocks, then keep splitting the widest gap. Each depth takes a prefix, spread through the stack.
Most steps train the full model. Otherwise one depth is drawn at random, and only its blocks run.
That path learns from the labels and from the frozen full model, so shallow depths aren't trained on noise.

scenes.title: CQ2-bit: the cost of a weight
scenes.say: Weights are stored at two bits. A Hadamard rotation makes every group look alike, so one fixed codebook serves them all.

parts.note: a 2-bit index into the shared codebook

parts.say: Plus a sixteen-bit norm shared by a hundred and twenty-eight weights.

parts.note: embedding and lane gates stay at 4-bit
parts.say: Two point one two five bits, with embeddings and lane gates at four.

scenes.label: the shipped 20-layer file, against a stated 29 MB ceiling
scenes.note: a flat 2.125 bits already gives 32.15 MB
scenes.say: Even a flat two point one two five bits overshoots the page's twenty-nine megabytes. The shipped twenty-layer file measures thirty-five point three four.

scenes.text: A sliceable model is trained, not cut. Shallow slices still need fine-tuning on your own tools to be useful.
scenes.say: A sliceable model is trained, not cut. Shallow slices still need fine-tuning on your tools to be useful.

recap: One sampled depth per step, distilled from the full model
CQ2-bit: 2.125 bits per weight, plus 4-bit extras
scenes.say: To recap: a bisected block order, one sampled depth per step with self-distillation, and two-bit weights on one codebook.
